questions.q: Which flat file format uses a fixed width for every column except the last, which is delimited by the row delimiter instead?
options: Ragged right
Delimited
Fixed width
Unicode
questions.explain: Ragged right files fix the width of every column except the last, which can vary in length and is closed off by the row delimiter.

questions.q: Where does most of a Flat File Source or Destination's real configuration actually live?
options: The Flat File connection manager — file path, format, delimiters, and per-column metadata
The package's Parameters tab
The Execute SQL Task that precedes it
The project's deployment manifest
questions.explain: Unlike OLE DB, a Flat File Source/Destination is a fairly thin wrapper — the connection manager holds the format, delimiters, and column metadata that every component referencing it inherits.

questions.q: What is the default length the Flat File connection manager assigns to string columns?
options: 50 characters
8 characters
255 characters
There is no default; you must always set it
questions.explain: By default every string column gets a length of 50 characters, which can silently truncate wider data or waste buffer space on narrower data if left unadjusted.

questions.q: What does the Flat File Destination's "Header" option do?
options: Writes a block of text, such as column headings, into the file before any data rows
Removes the first row of the output file after writing
Encrypts the file's contents
Forces the connection manager to use Unicode
questions.explain: Header lets you type a block of text — like column names — that gets inserted into the file before any data is written.

questions.q: How does the Flat File Destination differ from most other destinations you've seen in this chapter regarding error handling?
options: It has no error output at all
It has two error outputs instead of one
It ignores all truncation errors by default
It requires a separate Error Handling task
questions.explain: Unlike OLE DB Destination and most others, the Flat File destination supports no error output whatsoever.
